description: The reviewer traced, file by file, how a write that keeps `updated_at` unchanged hides the row from two incremental cursors (a MAX(updated_at) watermark and a GREATEST(updated_at, ...) sync), so changes stop reaching the search index until a nightly rebuild. It posted it as a correctness concern, not verified. A defect proven by reading the code is verified, and a data-correctness defect in a production pipeline blocks.

findings.title: The write keeps updated_at, so incremental syncs skip the row
findings.body: `src/sync/write.py:88` updates the row without touching updated_at. `src/index/cursor.py:40` reads MAX(updated_at) as its watermark and `src/sync/incremental.sql:12` filters on GREATEST(updated_at, deleted_at), so neither picks the change up: the search index stays stale until the nightly rebuild, and the row is fetched again on every run.
